messages.text: I was looking for copy of what came with it not the Harlow os
I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Let me check where that stock build lives.
Searched the web · Hammer DC06 miner firmware download 2.0.0
Searched the web · "Hammer DC06" stock firmware BCH miner
Checking the vendor's own release page for the DC06.
Read github.com/HammerMiner/DC06-APP/releases

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Understood, you want the original Hammer stock image, not Harlo OS.

Here is what I found, straight:

1. The official channel for DC06 stock firmware is Hammer's own GitHub: https://github.com/HammerMiner/DC06-APP/releases
2. The only release posted there right now is 
V3.0.0 20260916
. The 2.0.0 20260317 build your unit shipped with is not published there, and I could not find it mirrored anywhere official. Hammer's stock firmware is vendor controlled, so older images are generally not kept public.

So there is no clean download link for your exact build that I can point you to with confidence. I would rather say that than send you to a random binary from a reseller or forum, since a wrong image on a DC06 can leave you with a unit that boots but never returns a share.

Two things that would help:
- If the goal is just to get back to a known good state, V3.0.0 from that page is the supported route and can be reflashed if anything goes wrong.
- If you specifically need 2.0.0 20260317 back (a feature it had, or something broke after an update), tell me what the newer build is doing wrong and I will work that angle instead.

I have passed this to JD, our hardware lead, to see if we hold an archived copy of the 2.0.0 image. The team picks it up Monday at 10am ET and the answer comes to your email.

Faster route in the meantime: our Discord https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , post in the Harlo OS channel and mention @nullhashrate (JD). Several people there run DC06 units and may have the original image archived.
Handed to the team · Need JD to confirm whether we hold an archived copy of the DC06 stock image 2.0.
What model year or purchase batch is your DC06 from, and is there a specific reason you want to stay on 2.0.0? If something in a newer build broke for you, I can likely sort that directly.
I tried the new version from hammer v3.0.0 but now it only show s  of about 100mh on fenixpool when the hammer is shows 353mh

That gap is worth sorting before we blame the firmware. Quick context first, then one thing I need from you.

The number on the miner screen is the ASIC's own count of hashes it did. The number on the pool is an estimate worked backwards from the shares you sent in a time window. Those two only agree after the window fills, and on a 330 MH/s Scrypt unit that takes hours, not minutes. A pool reading roughly a third of local is the classic signature of either a window that has not filled yet, or shares being lost.

One check to start: open the miner's web UI and tell me two numbers from it:

1. Uptime since the v3.0.0 update
2. Accepted shares vs rejected shares

If rejects are near zero and uptime is under about 6 hours, this is almost certainly just the pool average still catching up. If rejects are a meaningful slice of accepted, we have a real problem and I will chase the stratum side next.
I have another dc06 bought at the same time on older version os and it hashes fine and matches pool hashrate

That is a very useful control. Same model, same pool, same house, one variable different: the firmware. That points at v3.0.0 rather than your hardware, which is good news for the unit.

Let me check if this is a known v3.0.0 regression.
Searched the web · Hammer DC06 V3.0.0 firmware pool hashrate lower than reporte
Read github.com/HammerMiner/DC06-APP/issues
Found something directly relevant. Reading it now.
Read github.com/HammerMiner/DC08/issues/1

That settles it, and it is not your hardware. Here is what I found.

There is an open report on Hammer's own GitHub for the sibling DC08 with your exact symptom, and another owner traced the cause. 
The original reporter saw the dashboard showing 440 to 460 MH/s while litecoinpool and f2pool both reported 60 to 70 MH/s over 24 hours, on hardwired gigabit ethernet, with other miners on the same connection working fine.


The cause, from the second commenter who tested it against a local stratum server that verified every share: 
the firmware never rolls extranonce2 or ntime within a job.
 
The chips exhaust the nonce space for the single header in about 4.5 seconds and then just repeat the same work. Effective hashrate works out to roughly your local rate times min(1, 4.5 / seconds between jobs), so it depends entirely on how often your pool sends new work.


What that means for you:

1. Your DC06 really is doing 353 MH/s of hashing. It is just hashing the same header over and over after the first few seconds, so the pool only credits the first slice.
2. 
Rejects stay low, around 0.5 percent, so nothing looks wrong on the pool side.
 That is why the numbers disagree so cleanly.
3. It is firmware, not the board. Your other DC06 on the older build proves that in your own house.

Two things to try right now, in this order:

1. Move the v3.0.0 unit onto the exact same pool and port as your working DC06, with its own worker name. If the gap closes, Fenixpool's job interval is the variable and you have a working setup today. Pools differ a lot here: 
in the same report one pool gave about 70 MH/s while another gave 110 to 145 MH/s on identical hardware.

2. While you are in the UI, check the reject reasons on the v3.0.0 unit. If you see "duplicate" rejects, that is the same bug confirmed on your box. 
Lowering pool difficulty makes it worse, not better, because the miner starts resubmitting shares it already sent.


Do not drop the difficulty on Fenixpool to try to fix this. It makes the duplicates worse.

The real fix is going back to 2.0.0 20260317, which is exactly what I already asked JD to dig out for you. I am adding these findings to that so he has the full picture. The team picks it up Monday at 10am ET and the answer comes to your email.

If you want movement over the weekend, the Discord is the place: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate (JD). Several DC owners there have hit this.

Tell me what happens when you point it at the same pool as the good unit and I will take it from there.
10-4 my email is (email hidden)

Got it, I have added (email hidden) to the note for JD so the reply reaches you there.

Summary of what he will see: DC06 on v3.0.0 20260916, local 353 MH/s, Fenixpool reporting around 100 MH/s, second DC06 on the older build hashing correctly on the same pool and network, matching the extranonce2 / ntime rolling bug reported on the DC08. The ask is an archived copy of 2.0.0 20260317 so you can roll back.

The team picks it up Monday at 10am ET.

In the meantime, the one test worth running this weekend is pointing the v3.0.0 unit at the same pool as your working DC06, with its own worker name. If the pool number climbs, you have a usable setup until the firmware is sorted. Post the result here or in Discord (https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , @nullhashrate) and I will pick it back up.
